title: Ethiopia’s Return to War Threatens to Engulf the Horn of Africa
gist: Ethiopia's Tigray civil war resumed in late September 2026 when the TPLF seized three airports and allied with six armed groups to oust Abiy Ahmed, after the 2022 Pretoria Agreement collapsed. Analysts fear Eritrea (newly freed from U.S. sanctions), Egypt and Sudan could be drawn in, turning the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb region into a tinderbox; the brief also covers Niger's uranium sovereignty push, a twentyfold surge in Sudanese refugees into Chad and Morocco's new PAM-led government.

insights.claim: Ethiopia's civil war resumed in late September 2026 when the TPLF seized three airports in Tigray and attacked Afar and Amhara, days after forming an alliance with six other armed groups to oust Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's federal government.
insights.so_what: Africa's second-most-populous country re-enters full-scale war, raising sovereign, humanitarian and regional-stability risk.
insights.quote: We are in the situation of full-blown war now
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: The renewed fighting coincides with a powerful El Niño threatening Ethiopian crop production, risking a broader humanitarian crisis.
insights.so_what: Compounding conflict and climate shocks raise food-insecurity and aid needs in the Horn.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: The 2020-2022 Tigray war killed an estimated 600,000 people and ended with the Pretoria Agreement, which has since collapsed over hard-liner grievances, the TPLF's ban from the June 2026 elections and the TPLF's May reestablishment of its prewar legislative council.
insights.so_what: Shows the peace deal's failure was a slow build, making the conflict likely protracted.
insights.quote: That conflict, which killed an estimated 600,000 people
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: ACLED data show the latest fighting began on Aug. 1 in Shererina near the Sudan border after months of troop buildup, escalating to all-out war only in late September.
insights.so_what: Conflict-data monitors gave roughly two months of warning before escalation.
insights.locator: The latest wave of fighting initially
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Ethiopia plans to withdraw more than 3,000 troops from Somalia to bolster domestic forces, potentially leaving a security vacuum that al-Shabab, increasingly working with the Houthis, could exploit.
insights.so_what: Tigray war could spill into Somali instability and Red Sea militant cooperation.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, Ethiopia is planning to withdraw
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Eritrea, which fought alongside Ethiopia in the last Tigray war, has now largely allied itself with the TPLF after being excluded from Pretoria talks and alarmed by Abiy's pursuit of Red Sea access through Eritrea.
insights.so_what: Realigned alliances raise the odds of an interstate Ethiopia-Eritrea war.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: In September 2026 the United States lifted sanctions on Eritrea's ruling party and military and ended an arms embargo on Ethiopia, hoping Asmara would join an alliance against Houthi Red Sea attacks given Assab port's proximity to Bab el-Mandeb.
insights.so_what: U.S. Red Sea security priorities may inadvertently fuel a Horn of Africa proxy war.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Lifting sanctions on Eritrea could push the still-sanctioned TPLF into ever-closer ties with Asmara and open a much larger proxy war; critics say it removes one of the few checks on state violence.
insights.so_what: Risk of second-order escalation from Western policy changes.
insights.quote: this decision [to lift sanctions] removes one of the few remaining checks on state-led violence
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Ethiopia's military chief Birhanu Jula accuses Egypt and Sudan of backing the new rebel alliance (including the Oromo Liberation Army and Amhara Fano), though there is no evidence and both deny it.
insights.so_what: Accusations alone raise interstate tension in an already crowded conflict zone.
insights.locator: Analysts also fear that Egypt and Sudan
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Egypt's dispute with Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and its alliance with Eritrea and Somalia, plus Sudanese army claims that Ethiopia helps the UAE arm the RSF, create overlapping rivalries.
insights.so_what: Nile water and Sudan war dynamics make the Tigray conflict a multi-state flashpoint.
insights.locator: Egypt has its own dispute with Ethiopia
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Overlapping alliances combined with Red Sea maritime instability from the war in Iran make the Tigray escalation a tinderbox for the entire Horn of Africa.
insights.so_what: Shipping through Bab el-Mandeb faces compounding risk from regional wars.
insights.quote: make the escalation of war in Tigray a tinderbox for the entire Horn of Africa
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Niger's prime minister told the UN General Assembly that Niger controls its uranium stockpiles and will sell supplies on the international market on its own terms.
insights.so_what: Signals resource nationalism affecting uranium supply chains historically tied to Europe.
insights.quote: For more than half a century, Niger’s uranium has lit the cities of Europe, while our cities have remained in darkness.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Nigeria and Ghana used UNGA to press for permanent African representation on the 15-member UN Security Council.
insights.so_what: Ongoing pressure for multilateral reform reflects shifting Global South leverage.
insights.quote: The world of 2026 cannot remain captive to the distribution of power in 1945
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: About 400 Sudanese per day are crossing into eastern Chad, a twentyfold increase over previous months driven by drone attacks and drought, with over 55,000 arrivals in 2026; Gen. al-Burhan rejected a U.S.-proposed three-month cease-fire with the RSF.
insights.so_what: Sudan's war is intensifying, not winding down, with spillover into the Sahel.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: Morocco's PAM won 97 of 395 seats; King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as Morocco's first female prime minister, while the previously ruling RNI fell to 66 seats after Gen Z-led protests over healthcare and unemployment.
insights.so_what: Youth discontent is reshaping North African politics; coalition government continues.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi

insights.claim: The Dangote Refinery has ended Nigeria's dependence on imported fuel but created a monopoly that suppresses local wages and resists regulation, according to an argument cited in the brief.
insights.speaker: Ayoola Babalola
insights.so_what: Nigeria's downstream oil self-sufficiency carries concentration and governance risk.
insights.quote: Nigeria’s development contradictions will not be resolved by one man’s industrial vision
